reviewer: independent training_auditor agent; not the probe author
review_type: static source and protocol-design review before diagnostic execution; not a measured gradient result

fixed_findings.issue: Original direction coverage required both analytic and numerical derivatives above the active-signal floor before checking summary success. A one-sided missing derivative could be omitted as inconclusive while another direction supplied tensor coverage.
fixed_findings.resolution: Every direction now must pass agreement and adjacent-scale stability at the two smallest epsilons before the signal floor classifies coverage. Disagreement remains a failure even when one or both derivatives are small.

fixed_findings.issue: Gradient tensor length was not checked before copying into allocated parameter-sized arrays.
fixed_findings.resolution: Gradient length must equal parameter length.

fixed_findings.issue: Tokenized sequence length lacked the trainer model-context bound.
fixed_findings.resolution: Every sequence is rejected if n_ids exceeds gf->ctx_len before capture.

fixed_findings.issue: Reported native joint scalar and independent oracle scalar had no acceptance gate.
fixed_findings.resolution: Scalar loss agreement is now required within 1e-4 times the sum of probe coefficients plus 1e-7.
Unit norm is checked to 1e-10 in squared norm and reported.

fixed_findings.issue: Initial epsilon-grid JSON used invalid leading decimal points.

verified_design: Production analytic gradient uses the current joint_loss and autograd implementation on four real cached Qwen targets.

The independent value oracle uses native C double arithmetic, direct LoRA matrix composition, stable sigmoid, RMS normalization with the production float epsilon promoted to double, and full-vocabulary log-sum-exp; it never calls backward.
Oracle perturbations affect double copies only; original parameters and cached/frozen float tensors have a before/after byte-change guard.
Native and oracle full logits and CE are compared separately for each of four targets, in addition to the joint scalar.
Each of six gate/up/down A/B tensors receives a maximum-gradient coordinate direction and a fixed-seed unit Rademacher direction at four epsilon values.
Two smallest epsilon values must agree with the analytic derivative and with each other; coarse-scale results remain visible.
Zero-B initialization expects exactly zero A derivatives; noninitial states require resolved derivative coverage for all six tensors.
The toy joint fixture now performs loss-only central finite differences at zero-B and nonzero-AB states, including all fixture parameters and a wrong-half-normalization rejection control.
limitations: The F64 oracle differentiates the intended smooth suffix function, not the piecewise-rounded F32 program.
Cached z, normalized input and base gate/up values are fixed inputs shared with production. This does not independently validate how attention or preceding layers produced those activations.
Only four globally weighted target contributions are tested: concern decision, clean decision, concern EOS and clean opening token. The full 1064-target gradient is not evaluated by this control.
Two directions per tensor do not exhaust all individual parameter derivatives.

A local derivative pass does not establish optimization convergence, full-network backward correctness, checkpoint selection quality, natural review quality or a mechanism for absent semantic transfer.
The toy fixture value oracle shares production forward CE and uses a single epsilon; its independence concerns backward/normalization checks, not a second full forward implementation.
No measurement outcome is asserted in this preflight audit.
interpretation_constraints: Weak held-out affine readout does not prove that semantic information never reaches the final token or that earlier layers alone would fix the task.
The saved update100 checkpoint merits a separately labeled repeated-holdout diagnostic because the original tie-break selected update25; do not replace the frozen original selection retrospectively.
